title: Ghost and Safehouse
premise: Wren Pemberton, a hostage negotiator who once lost a hostage and her reputation in the same afternoon, has spent three years buried in a quiet bureau desk, keeping a go-bag packed for a life she no longer trusts anyone to offer. When an encrypted invitation arrives from Marcus Hale—her former handler, dead for eleven months—she follows it to a decommissioned lighthouse safehouse and finds him alive, hunted by the very extraction cell he built to move witnesses out of the country. Hale holds proof that the hostage death Wren carries like a stone was orchestrated from inside the agency, and he needs her to negotiate his passage onto the dawn flight while the cell's cleaner closes in. To save them both she must trade the secret she's guarded longest—that she saw the orchestrator's face that night—for a future neither of them expected to survive; they make the flight, but only after Wren burns her career, exposes the orchestrator on an open channel, and chooses love against duty at the runway's edge.
about_author: Tamsin Montrose is a former crisis-line counselor who writes thrillers about people who talk their way out of impossible rooms. She lives on the Cornish coast, where she claims every lighthouse has a story it hasn't told yet.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Wren Pemberton's POV. Three years of careful invisibility shatter when an encrypted message arrives from her dead handler: coordinates, tomorrow, come alone. She checks the obituary again, hands shaking. Emotional beat: dread braided with a terrible, familiar hope.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter as Wren packs, revealing the failed negotiation that ended her field career—the hostage, Ada Voss, who died on her watch. Her partner Dev notices the bag and says nothing. Emotional beat: guilt as muscle memory.

chapters.title: Lighthouse at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Wren reaches the coastal safehouse at dusk and finds signs of occupation: fresh coffee, two cups. Someone knows her habits. She enters anyway. Emotional beat: the negotiator walking into her own hostage situation.

chapters.title: Dead Man Talking
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale's POV interleaved with the reunion. Hale is alive, half-healed, and explains the faked death: his witness-extraction network was compromised from inside. He needs one flight at dawn and one negotiator he trusts. Emotional beat: relief curdling into alarm.

chapters.title: The Voss File
chapters.summary: Hale shows Wren evidence that Ada Voss's death was engineered—a deliberate sacrifice to bury a mole trail. Wren's defining failure was someone else's design. Emotional beat: grief re-forged into fury.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: A drone passes over the lighthouse; the extraction cell has found the safehouse. Hale identifies the approaching cleaner as Sable, a man who never misses twice. They have until morning. Emotional beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She drafts a negotiation strategy—but the counterparty is the agency itself, reachable only through the mole she can now name: Deputy Director Corliss. To use the name is to spend her last protection. Emotional beat: weighing a secret worth killing for.

chapters.title: Sable Arrives
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, cold and procedural. He scouts the causeway, cuts the landline, and leaves a calling card on the door—a bullet casing from the night Voss died. Emotional beat: menace without a single raised voice.

chapters.title: Two Cups, One Truth
chapters.summary: Trapped together through the night, Wren and Hale trade confessions: why he faked his death, why she kept the go-bag packed. The old unspoken thing between them finally gets words. Emotional beat: love surfacing exactly when survival is least likely.

chapters.title: Open Channel
chapters.summary: Wren makes contact with the duty desk using Hale's cipher, posing as a middleman offering 'the Pemberton testimony' in exchange for safe passage. Somewhere in the building, Corliss reads the message. Emotional beat: the trap closing on both ends.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Summoned to Corliss's office, Dev realizes Wren is alive and being set up as the fall scapegoat for Voss. He must choose between reporting her or buying her time. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by paperwork and threat.

chapters.title: Causeway Rising
chapters.summary: The tide turns and Sable moves. Wren stalls him at the seawall using pure negotiation—buying minutes by making himself the audience to a confession he doesn't know is bait. Emotional beat: talking as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Hale reveals his insurance: everything, including Corliss's voice, is already aboard the extraction plane's secure server—if they reach it. But the flight requires a code only Corliss can issue. Emotional beat: hope with a razor edge.

chapters.title: Compromise
chapters.summary: Wren offers Corliss the deal directly: her silence about his face that night in exchange for the flight code. His counteroffer—Hale's head for hers—forces her to admit which secret she actually values. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated aloud.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Sable breaches the safehouse. A brutal close-quarters sequence; Hale takes a wound covering Wren's escape through the fog tunnel beneath the light. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into clarity.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Wren drags Hale through the tidal caves as the water rises, negotiating with herself—every reason to leave, every reason not to. Emotional beat: endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: Corliss Unmasked
chapters.summary: Cornered at the airfield perimeter, Wren plays her last card: she broadcasts the Voss file on the open channel Dev has quietly left unlocked. Agents hear the truth before Corliss can silence it. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid for in career blood.

chapters.title: Runway Standoff
chapters.summary: Sable, ordered to erase loose ends, faces Wren on the tarmac as the plane idles. She talks him down—not with mercy, but with the truth that Corliss will burn him too. Emotional beat: the negotiator's finest hour.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: Wounded but breathing, Hale boards. The code comes through—Corliss, arrested mid-betrayal, releases it as his final spite or final surrender. Wren hesitates at the stairs. Emotional beat: the choice made visible.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass
chapters.summary: Wren steps aboard, leaving her badge, her name, and her old life on the tarmac. Dev watches from the fence and lets her go. Emotional beat: grief and freedom indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Weeks later, somewhere unnamed. Wren and Hale rebuild the extraction network properly this time—with her rules, her ethics, her ledger of names. Emotional beat: purpose reborn from ruin.

chapters.title: Ada's Weather
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Wren's POV. At Voss's grave, Wren finally sets down the stone she's carried, telling Ada the truth and the outcome. The go-bag stays unpacked—for now. Emotional beat: the price of survival, paid in full and worth it.
